entries.label: SEL-001
entries.sub: Exclude a plain parallel key where the hub must slide under torque
entries.text: sel-001 exclude a plain parallel key where the hub must slide under torque if the required function is transmission of torque between shaft and hub and the operating context requires the mounted element to move axially while torque is transmitted, exclude the plain parallel key connection.

entries.label: SEL-002
entries.sub: Admit splines where the hub must slide under torque
entries.text: sel-002 admit splines where the hub must slide under torque if the required function is transmission of torque between shaft and hub and the context requires axial motion under torque, admit spline connections, provided the spline is specified with a fit that permits sliding.

entries.label: SEL-003
entries.sub: Flag friction-based connections when overload protection is required
entries.text: sel-003 flag friction-based connections when overload protection is required if a requirement of kind overload protection is present, flag every alternative whose torque transfer is purely frictional, because such a connection has no member intended to fail first. the rule flags rather than excludes: a friction joint can slip rather than break, which is itself a form of overload response. whether slipping is acceptable is a design judgement the sources do not settle.

entries.label: SEL-004
entries.sub: Prefer alternatives without a keyseat when shaft fatigue governs
entries.text: sel-004 prefer alternatives without a keyseat when shaft fatigue governs if shaft fatigue life at the connection is a governing requirement, prefer connections that do not require a keyseat in the shaft. a press fit is not free of stress concentration: shigley records a raiser in the shaft bending stress near the hub ends, with first estimates typically not greater than 2. the preference is comparative, not absolute.

entries.label: SEL-005
entries.sub: Restrict setscrew, pin, tapered-fit and press-fit connections to low torque
entries.text: sel-005 restrict setscrew, pin, tapered-fit and press-fit connections to low torque treat pins, setscrews in hubs, tapered fits and press fits as candidates for cases of low torque transmission.

entries.label: SEL-006
entries.sub: Prefer the involute spline form over the straight-sided form
entries.text: sel-006 prefer the involute spline form over the straight-sided form where a spline is selected, prefer the involute form. mott states this preference without attaching an operating context, so the rule carries context_unspecified rather than an invented one.

entries.label: SEL-007
entries.sub: Require a thrust-capable support where thrust load is present
entries.text: sel-007 require a thrust-capable support where thrust load is present if the support must carry a thrust load, exclude alternatives that do not perform the carry-thrust-load function. marked analyst-authored because the exclusion rests on the function assignments in this ontology, not on a cited statement that particular families cannot take thrust.

entries.label: SEL-008
entries.sub: Require manufacturer data for any real bearing selection
entries.text: sel-008 require manufacturer data for any real bearing selection any bearing selection intended for a real application must be closed against the specific manufacturer's published data, not against textbook tables.

entries.label: SUB-000
entries.sub: A shared function establishes at most a functional alternative
entries.text: sub-000 a shared function establishes at most a functional alternative if a candidate and a baseline both perform the preserved function, and nothing further is known, the verdict is functionalalternative. this is the ceiling that co-function alone can justify. encodes the definition of functionalalternative from ontology/core/substitution.ttl. not terminal: later rules may strengthen or weaken the verdict on evidence about context and interfaces.

entries.label: SUB-001
entries.sub: A candidate that cannot deliver the preserved function is not an alternative
entries.text: sub-001 a candidate that cannot deliver the preserved function is not an alternative if the candidate does not perform the preserved function in the stated context, or its interface is incompatible and no modification is offered, the verdict is notanalternative.

entries.label: SUB-002
entries.sub: A violated requirement in the stated context defeats substitution
entries.text: sub-002 a violated requirement in the stated context defeats substitution if the candidate violates a requirement that is applicable in the stated context, and that requirement expresses the reason the baseline was chosen, the verdict is notanalternative in that context. instantiated by sa-006: a parallel key violates the axial-motion requirement in a context that demands sliding under torque, so it is not an alternative there, even though it is one elsewhere.

entries.label: SUB-003
entries.sub: Named conditions or modifications yield a conditional verdict
entries.text: sub-003 named conditions or modifications yield a conditional verdict if the candidate preserves the function but only under stated conditions, or only after stated design modifications, the verdict is conditionallysubstitutable. the `requires` clause is not decoration; shacl enforces it, so a conditionallysubstitutable verdict with no condition and no modification fails validation.

entries.label: SUB-004
entries.sub: Direct substitutability requires positive interface and requirement evidence
entries.text: sub-004 direct substitutability requires positive interface and requirement evidence a verdict of directlysubstitutable may be reached only when the interface is identical, no applicable requirement is violated, no design modification is required, and the context conditions are unchanged. no assessment in v0.1 reaches this verdict. that is a finding, not a gap: every pair examined in the pilot requires at least a change of shaft or hub feature, so none is a drop-in replacement.

entries.label: SUB-005
entries.sub: Preference requires a stated requirement set
entries.text: sub-005 preference requires a stated requirement set a verdict of preferredalternative may be reached only when the candidate is at least conditionally substitutable and outperforms the baseline on a requirement that is applicable in the stated context. the preference is relative to that requirement set and is not a general ranking. instantiated by sa-001, where the spline is preferred because the context makes axial motion a requirement. change the requirement set and the preference disappears: shigley calls splines usually unnecessary for simple torque transmission.

entries.label: SUB-006
entries.sub: An unfixable threshold yields insufficient evidence
entries.text: sub-006 an unfixable threshold yields insufficient evidence if the applicability of a substitution turns on a qualitative threshold that no cited source quantifies, the verdict for automated evaluation is insufficientevidence, regardless of how well the alternatives otherwise match. instantiated by sa-003, whose applicability depends on 'low torque transmission'. the human-readable conditional verdict is retained; only automated evaluation degrades to insufficientevidence.

entries.label: SUB-007
entries.sub: Substituting across a load-life exponent boundary invalidates the baseline life calculation
entries.text: sub-007 substituting across a load-life exponent boundary invalidates the baseline life calculation when the candidate and the baseline belong to bearing families with different load-life exponents, any life or capacity comparison must be recomputed with the candidate's exponent. carrying the baseline's result across is invalid. both books give 3 for ball bearings and 3.33 or 10/3 for roller bearings. they also warn that the exponent is meaningless without the rating-life basis it was fitted against, which differs between manufacturers.

entries.label: SUB-008
entries.sub: Removing a sacrificial member is a loss of function, not a neutral change
entries.text: sub-008 removing a sacrificial member is a loss of function, not a neutral change if the baseline performs the limit-transmitted-torque function and the candidate does not, the substitution is not function-preserving even when torque capacity is equal or greater. guards against the common error of treating a stronger connection as strictly better. mott's shear pin and shigley's fusible key are both intended to fail.

entries.label: VER-001
entries.sub: A key connection requires both a shear check and a bearing check
entries.text: ver-001 a key connection requires both a shear check and a bearing check any parallel key connection must be checked for direct shear and for bearing (compressive) stress. where the two give different required lengths, the larger governs.

entries.label: VER-002
entries.sub: A keyed or splined shaft requires a stress-concentration assessment
entries.text: ver-002 a keyed or splined shaft requires a stress-concentration assessment where a keyseat, transverse hole or spline run-out is present in a shaft under cyclic loading, the stress concentration at that feature must be assessed as part of the shaft fatigue check.

entries.label: VER-003
entries.sub: An interference fit requires a pressure calculation at both tolerance extremes
entries.text: ver-003 an interference fit requires a pressure calculation at both tolerance extremes an interference-fit connection must be evaluated at both interference extremes: the maximum interference to check for excessive stress, and the minimum interference to bound the torque the joint may be designed to transmit without slipping.

entries.label: VER-004
entries.sub: A non-standardised keyless connection requires testing that neither book defines
entries.text: ver-004 a non-standardised keyless connection requires testing that neither book defines where a shaft/hub attachment method is not standardised and a satisfactory analysis is not possible, testing of the assembly is recommended.

entries.label: VER-005
entries.sub: A rolling bearing requires both a rating-life and a static-rating check
entries.text: ver-005 a rolling bearing requires both a rating-life and a static-rating check a rolling-contact bearing selection must be checked for rating life under the operating load and, separately, against the basic static load rating for the largest load applied while stationary or slow-moving.

entries.label: VER-006
entries.sub: A setscrew connection is verified against tabulated holding power with a load-type factor
entries.text: ver-006 a setscrew connection is verified against tabulated holding power with a load-type factor a setscrew connection is checked by comparing the applied axial or tangential load against tabulated holding power, derated by a factor of safety chosen for the loading type. the tabulated holding-power values themselves are not reproduced in this ontology; the rule cites their location.

entries.label: VER-007
entries.sub: A spline capacity calculation must respect its unit system and length basis
entries.text: ver-007 a spline capacity calculation must respect its unit system and length basis mott's sae straight-sided spline torque capacity is stated in inch units with torque in pound-inches, and is a capacity per inch of engaged spline length. it must be multiplied by the engaged length and must not be used in si without conversion. recorded as a verification rule rather than a note because silently applying this formula in si, or forgetting the per-inch basis, is a plausible and consequential error.

entries.label: Machine Elements in Mechanical Design
entries.sub: 6th ed. — Robert L. Mott, Edward M. Vavrek, Jyhwen Wang
entries.text: machine elements in mechanical design 6th ed. — robert l. mott, edward m. vavrek, jyhwen wang machine elements in mechanical design.pdf

entries.label: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design
entries.sub: 10th ed. — Richard G. Budynas, J. Keith Nisbett
entries.text: shigley's mechanical engineering design 10th ed. — richard g. budynas, j. keith nisbett ad7608c18e740b0e402c025fa3187de8.pdf

entries.label: SA-001
entries.sub: PreferredAlternative — Involute spline connection replaces Parallel key connection
entries.text: sa-001 preferredalternative — involute spline connection replaces parallel key connection replace a parallel key with an involute spline where the hub must slide under torque hub must slide axially along the shaft while transmitting torque both books support the direction of this conclusion from different angles: mott rules the key out for sliding service, shigley rules the spline in. neither book states the substitution as such; the conclusion is an analyst synthesis over two cited claims, and is marked needsreview.

entries.label: SA-002
entries.sub: ConditionallySubstitutable — Press-fit connection replaces Parallel key connection
entries.text: sa-002 conditionallysubstitutable — press-fit connection replaces parallel key connection replace a parallel key with an interference (press or shrink) fit on a permanently located hub hub permanently located, steady unidirectional torque, no field disassembly the decisive open item is the coefficient of friction f. shigley's equation is complete in form but the cited section does not fix f, so the torque capacity is not determinable from these two books alone. that is recorded as a gap requiring manufacturer data or test, not filled with a textbook value from elsewhere.

entries.label: SA-003
entries.sub: ConditionallySubstitutable — Setscrew connection replaces Parallel key connection
entries.text: sa-003 conditionallysubstitutable — setscrew connection replaces parallel key connection replace a parallel key with a setscrew connection at low torque low torque, hub position adjusted during assembly, cost-driven the conclusion is conditional on a threshold the sources decline to fix. the assessment is therefore usable as guidance but cannot be executed as a rule without an externally supplied torque boundary.

entries.label: SA-004
entries.sub: ConditionallySubstitutable — Multiple parallel key connection replaces Parallel key connection
entries.text: sa-004 conditionallysubstitutable — multiple parallel key connection replaces parallel key connection replace a single parallel key with two keys where the hub length limits key length required key length exceeds the available hub length a frequently made and rarely justified assumption is that two keys each carry half the torque. neither cited source says so. the assessment records the gap instead of assuming equal sharing.

entries.label: SA-005
entries.sub: NotAnAlternative — Cylindrical roller bearing replaces Single-row deep-groove ball bearing
entries.text: sa-005 notanalternative — cylindrical roller bearing replaces single-row deep-groove ball bearing replace a deep-groove ball bearing with a cylindrical roller bearing under combined radial and thrust load shaft support carrying combined radial and thrust load included to show a notanalternative verdict resting partly on an ontology function assignment rather than wholly on cited text, and to show that such a verdict is flagged as evidence-limited rather than presented as textbook-supported. note also that substituting between bearing families changes the load-life exponent (3 for ball, 10/3 for roller), so a capacity comparison cannot reuse the baseline's life calculation.

entries.label: SA-006
entries.sub: NotAnAlternative — Parallel key connection replaces Involute spline connection
entries.text: sa-006 notanalternative — parallel key connection replaces involute spline connection replace an involute spline with a parallel key where the hub must slide under torque (reverse of sa-001) hub must slide axially along the shaft while transmitting torque deliberately paired with sa-001 to demonstrate that the model does not treat substitutability as symmetric. the spline replaces the key here; the key does not replace the spline. a graph that inferred the reverse edge automatically would assert something both sources contradict.

entries.label: design factor
entries.text: design factor closematch design factor n design factor n_d both denote the ratio by which strength exceeds the stress or load a part must carry. symbols differ. shigley additionally reserves a second symbol for the value actually achieved after design; mott does not.

entries.label: achieved safety margin after the design is fixed
entries.text: achieved safety margin after the design is fixed differsinterminology design factor (no separate term) n factor of safety n shigley distinguishes the a-priori design factor n_d from the as-built factor of safety n, which generally differs numerically because of rounding to standard sizes. mott uses one symbol n throughout. readers moving between the books must not assume n and n are interchangeable.

entries.label: rolling-bearing load/life exponent
entries.text: rolling-bearing load/life exponent exactmatch load/life exponent k load-life exponent a same physical exponent, different symbol. values agree for ball bearings (3.00 and 3); for roller bearings mott prints the rounded decimal 3.33 and shigley the exact fraction 10/3. the symbols are deliberately not merged in the graph.

entries.label: load applied to a rolling bearing
entries.text: load applied to a rolling bearing differsinterminology load p load f same quantity, different symbol. note the collision risk: shigley uses p elsewhere for force, pressure and diametral pitch, so symbol-level merging across the two books would be actively wrong.

entries.label: load-life relation for rolling bearings
entries.text: load-life relation for rolling bearings closematch relationship between bearing load and life, l2/l1 = (p1/p2)^k eq. 14-1 load-life regression, f l^(1/a) = constant eq. 11-1 algebraically equivalent statements of the same power law, written in different forms: mott as a ratio between two operating points, shigley as an invariant of the fitted line. equivalence holds only when the exponent and the rating-life basis are matched.

entries.label: rating life at 90 percent survival
entries.text: rating life at 90 percent survival refines rated life / l10 life l10 rating life (also minimum life, l10 life, b10 life) l10 shigley gives the fuller definition, attributes the term to the abma, enumerates the synonyms, and locates it as the 10th percentile of the revolutions-to-failure distribution. shigley refines mott here rather than disagreeing with it.

entries.label: basic dynamic load rating
entries.text: basic dynamic load rating closematch basic dynamic load rating c catalog load rating / basic dynamic load rating c10 shigley's subscript 10 marks the tie to the 10 percent failure fraction, and shigley notes the name basic dynamic load rating applies specifically when the manufacturer's rating life is one million revolutions. mott's c carries the same meaning but assumes that basis silently.

entries.label: groove receiving a key
entries.text: groove receiving a key differsinterminology keyseat (shaft and hub); keyway used commonly for the hub groove — keyseat; keyway depth — mott explicitly notes that the hub groove is usually called a keyway but is more properly also a keyseat. the ontology keeps one class and records both surface forms as labels rather than picking a winner.

entries.label: spline
entries.text: spline closematch a series of axial keys machined into a shaft, with corresponding grooves in the bore of the mating part — essentially stubby gear teeth formed on the outside of the shaft and inside of the hub — same element, two framings. mott frames the spline as a multiplied key, shigley as a shortened gear. the framings foreshadow their differing emphases: mott stresses load sharing, shigley stresses manufacturing cost.

entries.label: yield strength
entries.text: yield strength exactmatch yield strength s_y yield strength s_y same property; mott uses lower-case s for strengths and shigley upper-case s. a purely notational difference, but one that breaks naive symbol matching across the two books.

entries.label: failure modes of a key
entries.text: failure modes of a key exactmatch shear across the shaft/hub interface; compression due to bearing action — direct shear; bearing stress — the two books identify the same two failure modes for a key in the same order. one of the clearest agreements in the pilot.

entries.label: torque capacity of a friction-based shaft/hub connection
entries.text: torque capacity of a friction-based shaft/hub connection relatednotequivalent keyless hub-to-shaft connection using a compressed steel ring (proprietary locking assembly) — interference fit torque capacity, t = (pi/2) f p l d^2 eq. 7-49 both concern friction-based torque transfer at a pressurised shaft/hub interface, but shigley supplies a closed-form capacity model for a plain interference fit while mott describes a proprietary ring assembly and directs the reader to the manufacturer. not interchangeable as a basis for calculation.
